newsitem.title: BELGIUM: EU opens probe into GAN's new rescue plan.
newsitem.headline: EU opens probe into GAN's new rescue plan.

text.p: The European Commission said on Wednesday it had started a probe into France's proposed plan to grant up to 20 billion francs to state-controlled insurer GAN to prepare it for privatisation.

Only in September last year, the Commission approved a 2.8-billion-franc state recapitalisation of GAN in 1995 on the assumption that the firm would divest its majority stake in bank Credit Industriel et Commercial (CIC) before being itself sold off.

But the French state jumped to the rescue of the troubled insurer again last month announcing it would make a capital injection of 11 billion francs to avoid a deterioration of its financial situation. Another nine billion would be to cover estimated losses.

GAN, whose problems stem mainly from its UIC property lending unit, is expecting to post a net attributable loss of five billion francs for 1996. The group suffered a loss of 1.8 billion in 1995 and 5.3 billion the previous year.

The Commission must vet all national governments plans to rescue ailing, often state-owned, companies. It normally is more enclined to approve such plans if limited to restore the long-term viability of the aided companies and if privatisation is in sight.
French Finance Minister Jean Arthuis said in February that the government planned to privatise GAN along with CIC "during the course of 1997".
